Comment class: other

Merged. [`420454c`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/commit/420454c) is on `main`, squashed, [#774](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/774) closed, local `main` synced and the conversation captured.

**The method now carries what the two rewrites taught**, so a future session writing rules gets these without a review round:

- a rule reached **while debugging** keys to the symptom, not the act
- a rule **correcting a misconception** keys to what the reader wants, not the wrong move
- a subject needing a **"that" pointing back** is a clause, not a situation — don't split it out
- past ~15 rules, **group under headings** by surface
- when grouping separates two rules that qualify each other, **add a pointer** — the one addition a rewrite may make, and one to declare when reporting

`chrome-extension/RULES.md` landed alongside as the worked example: 14 bullets → 24 rules in 6 sections, 52 technical facts audited present.

**What the experiment actually established**, beyond the four lessons: a session with no context, no format named and no skill named produced the house shape from the corpus alone. That's the property you were testing, and it held. The failure mode I predicted — the skill's description not naming a pack's `RULES.md` — didn't occur, so I left the description alone rather than adding a guard against something that hasn't gone wrong.

The sharpest moment was mechanical rather than editorial: my build script asserted every subject opened with an act, and it **rejected** the symptom-keyed trigger when I merged the better version in. The old rule was encoded in a check, and the check refused. That's what turned a matter of taste into a finding.

Still open: [#777](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/777) (the chrome-extension README claiming a prose rule that never existed — your call between correcting the table and writing the rule) and [#766](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/766) (the remaining `RULES.md` files under the line-length advisory).

# chrome-extension pack

Active when a `manifest.json` declares `manifest_version` — the MV3 build/runtime gotchas that apply while you're *coding* an extension. Mostly prose (`RULES.md`); the gotchas with a static signature in the source are checks.

Releasing and Chrome-Web-Store publication are a separate, opt-in concern: the [`chrome-extension-release`](../chrome-extension-release/README.md) pack (its `RELEASE.md` standard + conformance checks), declared when the project is ready to ship.

## Prose gotchas (`RULES.md`)

| Rule (≤5 words) | How enforced |
|---|---|
| MV3 worker paths must be root-absolute | prose |
| SetIcon needs imageData, not path | prose + check (`declarative-content-set-icon`) |
| Injected shared global: augment, not replace | prose |
| CDP-introspecting an MV3 worker traps | prose |
| JWT auth via launchWebAuthFlow id_token | prose |
| MV3 loads ES modules natively | prose |
| Content scripts are classic, not modules | prose + check (`content-script-module-syntax`) |
| Silent token refresh needs prompt=none | prose |
| host_permissions does not bypass CORS | prose |

The table over-claimed, as you called it. Fixing the row alone would have left the cause in place, so this removes the index instead.

## What was wrong

`packs/chrome-extension/README.md` carried a nine-row index of `RULES.md`'s rules. One row read `SetIcon needs imageData, not path — prose + check`, but no such prose rule has ever been committed — `git log -S imageData` finds none. The check's `doc` pointed at `RULES.md` as well, so a reader following a finding landed on a file that never explained it.

The index was stale a second way, which the first fix wouldn't have touched: it listed **nine** of the file's rules, and after #775 the file has **twenty-four**.

## The fix

The index is gone. `README.md` now points at `RULES.md` and names its six sections, and keeps a two-row table of the gotchas this pack also enforces with a check — the one fact the README holds that `RULES.md` doesn't.

That's the repo's own rule about a file that references another: state what you need from it, don't re-spell what it says. `packs/README.md` names this exact failure — *"A README that restates the manifest is duplication with a drift risk, and several had already drifted"* — and this table was an instance of it, drifting in both directions at once.

`declarative-content-set-icon` keeps a `doc`, now pointing at the README, which states that this rule is carried by the check alone. I first dropped the field, since it's optional in the schema — but `--list` then showed it as the only check in the catalog with no doc, so pointing it somewhere true is better than pointing it nowhere.

## Verification

- 1417 tests pass; `check_the_world` reports 0 blocking
- the catalog lists a real doc for every check, `declarative-content-set-icon` included

Closes #777

input.commit_message:
The README carried a nine-row index of RULES.md's rules, and it had
drifted: one row claimed "SetIcon needs imageData — prose + check" when no
such prose rule has ever been committed. The check's doc pointed at
RULES.md too, so a reader following a finding landed on a file that didn't
explain it. The index was stale a second way as well, listing nine of the
file's rules where there are now twenty-four.

The index is replaced by a pointer to RULES.md and its section names, plus
a two-row table of what this pack enforces with a check — the one fact the
README holds that RULES.md doesn't, and the part that can't drift per-rule.

declarative-content-set-icon keeps a doc pointer, now at the README, which
states that this rule is carried by the check alone.

Closes #777
